title: Water Bottles II
summary: Given the initial count of full water bottles and the number of empty bottles required for an exchange, determine the maximum number of water bottles that can be drunk.
statement: Given the initial count of full water bottles and the number of empty bottles required for an exchange, determine the maximum number of water bottles that can be drunk. In each operation, you can either drink any number of full bottles or exchange a specified number of empty bottles for one full bottle, increasing the exchange requirement after each exchange.
constraints: num_bottles and num_exchange are positive integers.
Drinking a full bottle creates one empty bottle; exchanging the current required number of empties produces one full bottle.
After each exchange the requirement increases by one; return the maximum total bottles drunk.
hints: Drinking immediately never hurts because full bottles only become the empties required for future exchanges.
Track empties, total consumed, and the increasing exchange requirement; perform one exchange whenever affordable.
Initialize consumed=empties=numBottles; while empties≥requirement: pay requirement, increment it, drink the new bottle, and add its empty.
Each exchange is forced and increases resources only through its returned empty, so the loop performs every possible exchange and stops exactly when none remains affordable.
editorial: Each exchange is forced and increases resources only through its returned empty, so the loop performs every possible exchange and stops exactly when none remains affordable.

tests.explanation: Drink thirteen, exchange six empties for one drink, then exchange seven of the eight empties for one more, totaling fifteen.
Successive requirements three, four, and five allow three additional bottles, for thirteen total.
